metadata.note: Santa Fe's San Diegan on the coastal Surf Line, the direct historical predecessor of Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner. Route geometry is taken from the modern Amtrak route's own GTFS-sourced alignment for this corridor (see amtrak.geojson), since the historical train ran the same physical line; where the historical train ran beyond or differently from today's Amtrak route, that is described in the segment notes. Era boundaries follow real, sourced milestones; headway_min and avg_speed_kmh within each era are estimates, not from real timetables.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: The San Diegan launched Mar 27 1938 with all-lightweight stainless Budd cars, one trainset making two round trips a day over the 128-mile Surf Line in 2h45m, timed to connect at Los Angeles with the Super Chief and the Chief. estimated; frequency not sourced from a real timetable
